54195-grit-or-the-young-boatman-of-pine-.title: The Young Boatman of Pine Point
54195-grit-or-the-young-boatman-of-pine-.creator: Horatio Alger, Jr.
54195-grit-or-the-young-boatman-of-pine-.description: A book by Horatio Alger, Jr.. Your stepfather had a good mercantile position in Boston, and we occupied a comfortable cottage in Newton. For some years all went well, but then I began to see a change for the worse in him. He became fond of drink, was no longer attentive to business, picked up bad associates, and eventually lost his position. This was when you were ten years of age. Then he took possession of my little capital and went into business for himself.

7843-the-happy-end.title: The Happy End
7843-the-happy-end.creator: Joseph Hergesheimer
7843-the-happy-end.description: A book by Joseph Hergesheimer. A gaunt young man with clear blue eyes sat on the bank of a mountain road and gazed at the newly-built house opposite. It was the only dwelling visible. Behind, the range rose in a dark wall against the evening sky; on either hand the small green valley was lost in a blue haze of serried peaks.

arxiv-1707-09579.title: The SNPR neighbourhood of tree-child networks
arxiv-1707-09579.creator: Jonathan Klawitter
arxiv-1707-09579.description: Abstract Network rearrangement operations like SNPR (SubNet Prune and Regraft), a recent generalisation of rSPR (rooted Subtree Prune and Regraft), induce a metric on phylogenetic networks. To search the space of these networks one important property of these metrics is the sizes of the neighbourhoods, that is, the number of networks reachable by exactly one operation from a given network.

arxiv-2005-04958.title: Persistence analysis of velocity and temperature fluctuations in convective surface layer turbulence
arxiv-2005-04958.creator: Subharthi Chowdhuri, Tamás Kalmár-Nagy, Tirtha Banerjee
arxiv-2005-04958.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Subharthi Chowdhuri, Tamás Kalmár-Nagy, Tirtha Banerjee. Persistence is defined as the probability that the local value of a fluctuating field remains at a particular state for a certain amount of time, before being switched to another state. The concept of persistence has been found to have many diverse practical applications, ranging from non-equilibrium statistical mechanics to financial dynamics to distribution of time scales in turbulent flows and many more.

arxiv-2012-13239.title: Linear complementary pair of group codes over finite principal ideal rings Corresponding author.
arxiv-2012-13239.creator: Hualu Liu
arxiv-2012-13239.description: Abstract A pair ( C , D ) (C,D) of group codes over group algebra R ⁡ [ G ] R[G] is called a linear complementary pair (LCP) if C ⊕ D = R ⁡ [ G ] C\oplus D=R[G] , where R R is a finite principal ideal ring, and G G is a finite group.

arxiv-2109-10680.title: rSVDdpd: A Robust Scalable Video Surveillance Background Modelling Algorithm
arxiv-2109-10680.creator: Subhrajyoty Roy, Ayanendranath Basu, Abhik Ghosh
arxiv-2109-10680.description: Abstract A basic algorithmic task in automated video surveillance is to separate background and foreground objects. Camera tampering, noisy videos, low frame rate, etc., pose difficulties in solving the problem. A general approach that classifies the tampered frames, and performs subsequent analysis on the remaining frames after discarding the tampered ones, results in loss of information.

arxiv-2205-04408.title: Efficient and flexible estimation of natural mediation effects under intermediate confounding and monotonicity constraints
arxiv-2205-04408.creator: Kara E. Rudolph, Iván Díaz
arxiv-2205-04408.description: Abstract Natural direct and indirect effects are mediational estimands that decompose the average treatment effect and describe how outcomes would be affected by contrasting levels of a treatment through changes induced in mediator values (in the case of the indirect effect) or not through induced changes in the mediator values (in the case of the direct effect).

arxiv-2210-04778.description: Abstract . We introduce 3 3 -dimensional generalizations of Postnikov’s plabic graphs and use them to establish cluster structures for type A A braid varieties. Our results include known cluster structures on open positroid varieties and double Bruhat cells, and establish new cluster structures for type A A open Richardson varieties.

arxiv-2505-02269.title: Information geometry and entanglement under phase-space deformation through nonsymplectic congruence transformation
arxiv-2505-02269.creator: Shilpa Nandi, Pinaki Patra
arxiv-2505-02269.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Shilpa Nandi, Pinaki Patra. The Fisher-Rao (FR) information matrix is a central object in multiparameter quantum estimation theory. The geometry of a quantum state can be envisaged through the Riemannian manifold generated by the FR-metric corresponding to the quantum state. Interestingly, any congruence transformation G ​ L ​ ( 2 ​ n , ℝ ) GL(2n,\mathbb{R}) in phase space leaves the FR-distance for Gaussian states invariant. In the present paper, we investigate whether this isometry affects the entanglement in the bipartite system.

arxiv-2511-07926.title: CNN-Based Automated Parameter Extraction Framework for Modeling Memristive Devices
arxiv-2511-07926.creator: Akif Hamid, Orchi Hassan*
arxiv-2511-07926.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Akif Hamid, Orchi Hassan*. Resistive random access memory (RRAM) is a promising candidate for next-generation nonvolatile memory (NVM) and in-memory computing applications. Compact models are essential for analyzing the circuit and system-level performance of experimental RRAM devices. However, most existing RRAM compact models rely on multiple fitting parameters to reproduce the device I–V characteristics, and in most cases, as the parameters are not directly related to measurable quantities, their extraction requires extensive manual tuning, making the process time-consuming and limiting adaptability across different devices.

arxiv-2512-18525.title: A Formal Descriptive Language for Learning Dynamics A Five-Layer Structural Coordinate System
arxiv-2512-18525.creator: Miyuki T. Nakata
arxiv-2512-18525.description: Abstract Understanding learning as a dynamic process is challenging due to the interaction of multiple factors, including cognitive load, internal state change, and subjective evaluation. Existing approaches often address these elements in isolation, limiting the ability to describe learning phenomena within a unified and structurally explicit framework. This paper proposes a multi-layer formal descriptive framework for learning dynamics.

pmc-11480419.title: Mitophagy related diagnostic biomarkers for coronary in-stent restenosis identified using machine learning and bioinformatics
pmc-11480419.creator: Ming Shen, Meixian Chen, Yu Chen, Yunhua Yu
pmc-11480419.description: Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) combined with stent implantation is currently one of the most effective treatments for coronary artery disease (CAD). However, in-stent restenosis (ISR) significantly compromises its long-term efficacy. Mitophagy plays a crucial role in vascular homeostasis, yet its role in ISR remains unclear. This study aims to identify mitophagy-related biomarkers for ISR and explore their underlying molecular mechanisms.

pmc-11487065.title: Generation of squeezed vacuum state in the millihertz frequency band
pmc-11487065.creator: Li Gao, Li-ang Zheng, Bo Lu, Shaoping Shi, Long Tian, Yaohui Zheng
pmc-11487065.description: The detection of gravitational waves has ushered in a new era of observing the universe. Quantum resource advantages offer significant enhancements to the sensitivity of gravitational wave observatories. While squeezed states for ground-based gravitational wave detection have received marked attention, the generation of squeezed states suitable for mid-to-low-frequency detection has remained unexplored.

pmc-11626457.title: Community-associated methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus in the Kimberley region of Western Australia, epidemiology and burden on hospitals
pmc-11626457.creator: Lauren Edna Bloomfield, Geoffrey Coombs, Paul Armstrong
pmc-11626457.description: This study presents surveillance data from 1 July 2003 to 30 June 2023 for community-associated methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (CA-MRSA) notified in the Kimberley region of Western Australia (WA) and describes the region’s changing CA-MRSA epidemiology over this period. A subset of CA-MRSA notifications from 1 July 2003 to 30 June 2015 were linked to inpatient and emergency department records.

pmc-12559729.creator: Guillaume Gricourt, Jean-Loup Faulon
pmc-12559729.description: The application of artificial intelligence in cheminformatics highlights the necessity of comprehensive datasets that fully utilize all available chemical information. While generalist databases such as PubChem provide extensive compound coverage, specialised resources such as Rhea, which relies on the ChEBI ontology, are critical for the study of enzyme-catalysed reactions.

pmc-12593275.title: Assessment of engineered sustainable nitrogen fertilizers on lettuce development using physical sampling and image‐based phenotyping
pmc-12593275.creator: Julia Farias, Matthew Conley, Matthew T. Herritt, Carson Call, Mohamed Ammar, Mohamed Eisa, Mariana Govoni Brondi, Jonas Baltrusaitis, Reagan W. Hejl, Clinton F. Williams
pmc-12593275.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Efficient and sustainable nitrogen (N) management is critical for addressing the dual challenges of maximizing productivity and mitigating environmental impacts in short‐cycle crops like lettuce (Lactuca sativa). This study evaluates the agronomic performance and nutrient dynamics of eight N fertilizer treatments, including mechanochemically synthesized urea‐based cocrystals, conventional urea, and mechanochemically synthesized carbonate salts alongside accessible digital phenotyping methods for a greenhouse‐grown romaine lettuce system.

pmc-12634000.title: Barriers and motivators experienced by South Asian primary care physicians in conducting research
pmc-12634000.creator: Waseem N. Ahmed, Marriam Sheraz, Sankha Randenikumara, Hina Jawaid, Nusrat Jahan, Md Ferdous Rahman, Ramakrishna Prasad, Swaathi Balasubramanian
pmc-12634000.description: Introduction:Research in primary healthcare is vital for improving clinical practices, health outcomes, and policy effectiveness. Despite recognizing its importance and willingness to conduct it many general practitioners face barriers in doing it.Objectives:Our study aimed to understand the challenges in conducting research and identify factors that motivate research culture among primary care physicians in South Asia.

pmc-12638985.title: Key features of the innate immune response is mediated by the immunoproteasome in microglia
pmc-12638985.creator: Salman Izadjoo, Kasey E Moritz, Guzal Khayrullina, Elizabeth M Bergman, Brendan M Melvin, Matthew W Stinson, Summer G Paulson, Nikki M McCormack, Kelsey N Anderson, Lunndon A Lewis, Jeremy D Rotty, Barrington G Burnett
pmc-12638985.description: Microglia are the resident immune cells of the central nervous system (CNS). We and others have shown that the inflammatory response of microglia is partially regulated by the immunoproteasome, an inducible form of the proteasome responsible for the generation of major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I epitopes.

pmc-13110468.title: Postmenopausal osteoporosis and vascular calcification: The estrogen regulation network and calcification paradox
pmc-13110468.creator: Yanxia Lin, Pengcheng Jiang, Yang Lv, Wen Tian
pmc-13110468.description: The decline in estrogen levels in postmenopausal women is a major risk factor for the high prevalence of osteoporosis and vascular calcification in this population. Estrogen deficiency leads to an imbalance in the RANKL/OPG ratio, abnormalities in the Wnt/β-catenin pathway, and disruptions in bone morphogenetic protein (BMP) signaling, thereby inducing osteoporosis and vascular calcification.

pmc-13186009.title: Transient epigenetic changes promote cardiomyocyte differentiation of the subcutaneous adipose stromal vascular fraction
pmc-13186009.creator: Yusuke Shinjo, Shinichiro Takashima, Chiaki Goten, Oto Inoue, Daiki Hashimuko, Kosei Yamaguchi, Yusuke Takeda, Kenji Sakata, Masayuki Takamura, Soichiro Usui
pmc-13186009.description: IntroductionThe subcutaneous adipose-tissue-derived stromal vascular fraction (Sa-SVF) contains stem/progenitor cells that rarely transdifferentiate into beating cardiomyocytes. Previously, we developed a culture protocol in which adult murine inguinal Sa-SVF cells reproducibly transdifferentiate into beating cardiomyocyte-like cells (beating CMs) without any specific induction in the primary culture. However, the mechanism underlying the differentiation of the Sa-SVF toward the cardiac lineage is unclear.

pmc-13276623.description: This cohort study describes the outcome of 2 text messaging interventions to reach patients eligible for government benefits programs. Introduction Public benefits help families obtain food, housing, and financial support that can address health-related social needs (HRSNs).1 In the US, despite recent funding cuts and eligibility restrictions, many households remain eligible to receive benefits but are not enrolled.

pmc-13301198.title: Local impedance based assessment of lesion effectiveness during pulsed field ablation using a variable-loop circular catheter
pmc-13301198.creator: M Kimura, Y T Toyama, S H Hamaura, M H Hiyama, Y I Ishida, T I Itoh, S S Sasaki, H T Tomita
pmc-13301198.description: BackgroundLocal impedance (LI) at the electrode–tissue interface is a promising surrogate of contact quality and lesion effectiveness during pulsed-field ablation (PFA).
